subject: general
question: The listed price of an article is Rs. 200. A customer purchases it at Rs. 150 after two successive discounts. If one discount is 10%, then the other discount percentage (rounded off to two decimal places) is:
solution:
**Given:**

Marked price of an article is Rs. 200 

Selling price of an article is Rs. 150 

One discount is 10% 

**Formula used:**

Discount = M.P - S.P 

Discount% = ((D)/(M.P)) × 100 

Where, D = discount, M.P = Marked Price 

S.P = Selling Price 

**Calculation:**

Here, we have marked price = Rs. 200, D = 10% 

As we know that d% = ((D)/(M.P)) × 100 

⇒ 10 = (d/200) × 100 

⇒ Discount = Rs. 20 

Also, S.P = M.P - Discount 

⇒ S.P after first discount = 200 - 20 = Rs. 180 

Also, after the second discount selling price is given as = Rs. 150 

Required discount% = ((180 - 150) )/(180 ) × 100 

⇒ ((30)/(180)) × 100 = 16.66%

**Hence, the required discount% is 16.66% .**
